question: In the “olist_geolocation” table, please identify which two consecutive cities, when sorted by geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, and geolocation_lng, have the greatest distance between them based on the difference in distance computed between each city and its immediate predecessor in that ordering.
sql:
WITH ordered_cities AS (
    SELECT 
        geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
        geolocation_lat,
        geolocation_lng,
        geolocation_city,
        geolocation_state,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) as rn
    FROM olist_geolocation
),
with_distances AS (
    SELECT 
        c1.geolocation_zip_code_prefix as zip1,
        c1.geolocation_lat as lat1,
        c1.geolocation_lng as lng1,
        c1.geolocation_city as city1,
        c1.geolocation_state as state1,
        c1.rn as rn1,
        c2.geolocation_zip_code_prefix as zip2,
        c2.geolocation_lat as lat2,
        c2.geolocation_lng as lng2,
        c2.geolocation_city as city2,
        c2.geolocation_state as state2,
        c2.rn as rn2,
        6371 * ACOS(
            GREATEST(-1, LEAST(1, 
                COS(RADIANS(c1.geolocation_lat)) * COS(RADIANS(c2.geolocation_lat)) * COS(RADIANS(c2.geolocation_lng - c1.geolocation_lng)) + 
                SIN(RADIANS(c1.geolocation_lat)) * SIN(RADIANS(c2.geolocation_lat))
            ))
        ) as distance
    FROM ordered_cities c1
    JOIN ordered_cities c2 ON c1.rn = c2.rn - 1
    WHERE c1.rn > 1
)
SELECT 
    city1,
    city2,
    state1,
    state2,
    rn1,
    rn2,
    distance
FROM with_distances
ORDER BY distance DESC
LIMIT 1
